newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to adopt 3-yr budget programme on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to adopt 3-yr budget programme on Friday.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Sunday his government would adopt a three-year budget "convergence programme" next Friday.

But speaking on Belgian RTBF television, Dehaene denied reports from the European Union's Dublin Summit that the programme aimed to cut the country's deficit to 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2000.
"I have never talked about 1.5 percent...thanks to our high primary surplus...the deficit will come down below three percent if interest rates stay where they are now," Dehaene said.
Dehaene reiterated the government has committed itself to maintaining its primary surplus at close to six percent of gross domestic product (GDP) into the next century.
The primary surplus is the difference between a government's revenues and spending, excluding the cost of debt financing.
"This automatically leads to a reverse snowball effect, bringing down our debt," Dehaene said.
Belgium must present the convergence programme to its European Union partners for comment in the New Year.
Under EU rules, each member state must regularly present three-year macro-economic forecasts which are judged by EU finance ministers.
Belgium's last convergence plan, which was revised in 1993, forecast budget deficits for 1994, 1995 and 1996 of 4.7 percent, 3.6 percent and 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The actual outurns for 1994 and 1995 were 5.1 percent and 4.1 percent. 1996's deficit is forecast by the government and central bank to be 3.3 percent.
